title: Palo Alto Networks firewall security
description: The firewall events a security team checks first: who changed policy, who logged in to the firewall, DNS sinkhole hits from infected hosts, threat detections, command-and-control traffic, and how threat volume trends over time.

splunkbaseApps.displayName: Splunk Add-on for Palo Alto Networks

requiredData.notes: Forward PAN-OS config, system, and threat logs to Splunk over syslog (or SC4S) with sourcetype pan:log; the Splunk Add-on for Palo Alto Networks splits them into pan:config, pan:system, and pan:threat. DNS sinkhole requires the DNS Security or anti-spyware sinkhole action.

industrySources.control: NIST SP 800-41 Rev. 1: firewall policy management and logging
Palo Alto add-on sourcetypes: pan:config (Change), pan:system (Authentication), pan:threat (Intrusion Detection)

curationNotes: Security only (pairId null): industry practice for firewalls has no distinct ops list a beginner can run on the default add-on.
Skips UC-5.2.9 and UC-10.1.2: they read pan:url and pan:wildfire, which the add-on does not emit (URL and WildFire events arrive as pan:threat subtypes).
Several steps are multi-vendor UCs; this pack uses their Palo Alto SPL.

No Cisco SD-WAN pack: catalogue SD-WAN UCs read cisco:sdwan:bfd/device/approute, while the Cisco Catalyst add-on emits cisco:sdwan:sitehealth/tunnelhealth/linkhealth. Revisit when UCs move to those sourcetypes.
